note: Where the competitors' links come from, which of those are reachable, and the correction that prompted this file. Domain ratings are Ahrefs, at the date above.
the_correction: This site's strategy had been resting on two examples of low authority domains outranking better ones, and both were misread. allmedicalwaste.com.au ranks seventh for sharps container at domain rating 3, and has 752 referring domains. aussiepeptidehub.com.au sits second for bacteriostatic water at domain rating 0, and has 270. A low domain rating does not stop either of them, which is the part that was right. Neither is a site with no links, which is the part that was wrong, and we have none at all. The gap between us and them is not that they are better regarded, it is that they exist in a few hundred places and we exist in zero.

channels.why: This is plainly the volume both rivals used. truelocal alone links to medshop 759 times. These are listings a supplier fills in, not favours anybody grants, and they are the cheapest way to stop being a domain with nothing pointing at it.

targets.evidence: not in the rival profile, but the standard Australian listing
not a link, but it is how a local pack entry starts and it is free

channels.why: The best links in medshop's profile and nobody would guess it. Nursing, paramedicine and dentistry programs publish the kit a student has to buy and who sells it. High domain rating, exactly on topic, and the lists are maintained by people whose job includes keeping them current. A supplier who prices clearly and ships without an account is genuinely useful to a first year student, which is the whole pitch.

channels.effort: low, mostly automatic once there is a live store
channels.why: These crawl Shopify and similar and list what they find. Not high quality individually and not nothing in aggregate, which is most of what the 752 behind allmedicalwaste looks like.
Worth knowing about and not worth starting with. These link when there is a story, and a consumables supplier with no products shipping yet does not have one.

channels.channel: The /learn guides pitched as reference, not as a supplier
channels.why: The only channel of the five that is not blocked on having something to sell, because it never asks anybody to list this business as a supplier. It asks them to link an explainer. Eight of the guides sit between position 5.9 and 10.4 at domain rating 0, which is the evidence that the writing is already good enough to be worth somebody's link, and the site has zero referring domains all time, so the first one is worth more than the tenth.

what_to_offer.audience: councils, state health sharps pages, needle and syringe programs
what_to_offer.why_they_link: Sharps disposal is a public health message they already publish. A plain explainer of what goes in a container and how to find a drop-off is the thing their page is usually missing.

what_to_offer.audience: nursing and paramedicine educators, diabetes educators
what_to_offer.why_they_link: Gauge runs backwards and every cohort of students asks. A single page that explains it is the kind of link a lecturer keeps.

what_to_offer.audience: practice managers, allied health and procurement blogs
what_to_offer.why_they_link: Most impressions of any page on the site, 79 in 28 days. What ARTG listing actually means is a question buyers ask and few pages answer without selling something.

channels.honest_yield: Cold outreach from a domain with no links converts in low single figures. Five links is a hundred emails, not ten. It is still the right first channel because it is the only one open, and because a link to a guide is a link to the domain.
channels.what_not_to_do: Do not pitch the shop, do not ask for a supplier listing, and do not offer anything in exchange for the link. The pitch is the guide or it is nothing.
channels.unverified: The named organisations below were not checked from this session: the sandbox cannot reach most of them. Confirm each has a resources or links section before sending, or the email is wasted.
targets_to_check: state health sharps disposal pages (NSW, VIC, QLD, WA, SA)
local council sharps disposal pages, which are numerous and the likeliest first win
university nursing and paramedicine subject guides

not_worth_it.why: Present in the rival profile and deliberately not listed as targets. Forum signatures, expired-domain junk and scraped mirrors: gamedev.place, webd.pl, prv.pl, tinhte.vn, mybluemix.net, itxoft.com. They are in medshop's profile because anybody's profile accumulates them, not because they were pursued. Chasing them is the thing that gets a domain rating of 3 on 752 links.

blocked_on.what: real products, real prices and a checkout
blocked_on.why: Every one of the four channels above asks a third party to list this business as a supplier of consumables. The catalogue is placeholder, the prices are indicative and there is no checkout, so all four would have us claim to a directory, a university or a trade publication something that is not true yet. That is the same rule the language gate enforces on the pages, and it does not stop applying because the claim is in an email instead of on a page.
so_the_order_is: Real products and real prices, which is the only thing that makes any of these four channels honest to pursue.
Then a Google Business Profile and the standard Australian listings, which are self-serve and need nobody to agree.
Then the university supplier lists, which are the best links in the rival profile and need an email each.
blocked_on.what_is_available_before_then: One thing, printed below. The guides under /learn are genuine reference content and can be offered as reference without any claim about the business, because offering an explainer asks nobody to list a supplier. The yield is low and it does not change the order above: on backlinks there is still no move that beats getting real stock on the site.
